description: The opening band of a page: headline, optional eyebrow/subheading, up to two CTAs, and optional media or trust-signal markup. Layouts: left, centered, split (text + media) and cover (tall, centred). REBUILT ON THE UNIVERSAL DESIGN CONTRACT (v2): it declares no style slots and no recipes. Every designable value — colour, type, spacing, border, shadow, size, crop — is set through the `udc` map on the band, per role. The CTA roles are the primary consumers of the `button` / `button-secondary` presets. See docs/v2/BUILD-SPEC-sprint0.md §3.

id.description: Optional HTML id attribute for anchor linking (e.g. navigation anchors).

title_accent.description: Optional exact substring of title to render in an accent color (e.g. one word or phrase). Must match title exactly (case-sensitive) or it is ignored and title renders normally.

eyebrow.description: Optional short kicker/label rendered as a pill above the title (e.g. "NEW", "PLUGIN OFICIAL").

subheading.description: Supporting subheadline shown below the title.

button_text.description: Primary CTA button label. Leave empty to hide both buttons.

button_url.description: Primary CTA button URL. Accepts an absolute URL, a site-relative /path, an #anchor, mailto:, or tel:; a disallowed protocol (javascript:, data:) is rejected at write time.

button2_text.description: Secondary CTA button label. Only shown when button_text is also set. Its look is the `cta-secondary` role, which ships the v1 outline treatment as its default — a muted surface with a border-coloured edge, distinct from the primary without any authoring. Override it through the `udc` map, or apply a different preset. The v1 `button2_variant` prop is gone: a variant was a bundle of colours, which is what a role default and a preset are.

button2_url.description: Secondary CTA button URL. Accepts an absolute URL, a site-relative /path, an #anchor, mailto:, or tel:; a disallowed protocol (javascript:, data:) is rejected at write time.

layout.description: Structural layout. centered centers all content. left aligns content left. split places text left and media right at lg+; if a split hero has neither an image (image_url/image_id) nor proof, there is nothing for the second column, so it degrades to the single-column left layout (text at full content width) — add an image or proof to get the two-column split. The degradation is RENDER-TIME ONLY: the stored prop is NOT rewritten, so reading the composition back still reports split while the page renders left. What follows the degraded layout is the root class and the split-scoped data attributes (split_ratio, vertical_align). cover is a TALL, CENTRED band (min-height 70vh): on v2 it no longer paints image_url as a background — set `_band` `background.image` (an attachment id) plus `background.overlay` for that, on any layout you like.

image_url.description: Image URL for the SPLIT layout's media column, rendered as an inline . On v2 this no longer paints a cover background: a band background image is `_band` `background.image`, an attachment id the engine resolves. Pair with image_id for a responsive srcset.

image_alt.description: Alt text for the split-layout image. Use a descriptive string for meaningful images; leave empty only if image is purely decorative.

image_id.description: Media Library attachment ID for the SPLIT layout's image (NOT a URL). When it resolves to a real attachment, the image renders responsively with srcset/sizes via wp_get_attachment_image() instead of a single fixed-size . Falls back to image_url when unset or unresolvable. Get an attachment id via the import_media apply. For a BAND BACKGROUND image, use the `_band` role's `background.image` instead.

split_ratio.description: Grid column ratio for the split layout. '60-40' gives more space to text, '40-60' gives more to the image. Ignored on non-split layouts.

vertical_align.description: Vertical alignment of content within the hero. Applies to cover and split layouts only. Ignored on centered/left layouts. Ignored below 1024px. 'stretch' is for the split layout: the media column fills the content column's height (equal-height columns) and the image sizes to that box with object-fit: cover, so one asset balances any headline length instead of a fixed-aspect card that dwarfs a tall headline. On the cover layout 'stretch' renders like 'center'.

proof.description: HTML string for trust signals (client logos, star ratings, user counts). Rich HTML (sanitized via wp_kses_post). Rendered after the CTA group inside hero__content, except on a split layout, where it renders instead as the second column inside the `.hero__surface` panel. That panel IS the `surface` role: style it through the `udc` map (background, border, radius, shadow, padding), not through style slots — hero has none. Write PLAIN SEMANTIC MARKUP here: the v1 `.hero__surface-label / -list / -item / -key / -value` helper classes are gone, so markup using those names paints nothing. Text inside the panel inherits the `surface` role's typography. When empty, no DOM element is rendered.

_band.description: The band itself — the <section>. Its own background, including a full-bleed background image and an overlay scrim, is set here. The v1 `cover` background came from `image_url`; on v2 it is `background.image` (an attachment id), which means ANY layout can carry one, not just `cover`.

inner.description: The row that holds the text column and, on a split layout, the media column. Its track geometry is structural; the space between the two columns is design.

content.description: The text column. Its measure lives here — this one role replaces the six interacting width mechanisms v1 had (#908).

eyebrow.description: The kicker pill above the headline.

title.description: The page headline (an <h1>). It declares NO colour and NO weight default, so it inherits both — set them here when the band's background or emphasis needs it. (The weight is deliberately left to base.css's shared h1-h6 rule: the theme's own --font-weight-heading is 650, which CSS Fonts 4 allows and this engine's font-weight grammar does not yet accept, so referencing it here would ship a default the validator refuses. Filed separately.)

title-accent.description: The accented substring inside the headline, rendered only when title_accent matches. Over a dark band or a background image, set this explicitly — the v1 cover variant used to re-colour it for you and v2 does not.

subtitle.description: The supporting line below the headline.

cta-group.description: The row the CTA buttons sit in. Its wrapping and alignment are structural; the space between the buttons is design.

cta.description: The primary CTA button. DECLARES NO DESIGN DEFAULTS ON PURPOSE: role defaults outrank presets, so a default here would suppress exactly the part of a `button` preset that makes it a button. Apply `"_preset": "button"` (or `button-secondary`, or your own values) and it lands whole. The v1 `button_variant` prop is gone — a variant was a bundle of colours, which is what a preset is.

cta-secondary.description: The second CTA button, rendered only when button2_text is set. CARRIES THE v1 OUTLINE DEFAULT, restored in v2 form (#986): a muted surface, body ink and a border-coloured 2px edge, every value a reference to a site token so a retheme moves it. Without it an unauthored hero rendered two identical filled buttons side by side, because both CTAs are bare `.btn` now that `button2_variant` is gone — a default-experience regression, not a narrowing worth documenting. These values are the `button-secondary` preset's, duplicated deliberately and temporarily: role defaults outrank presets, so applying a DIFFERENT preset to this role is partly suppressed by them until #974 lets a role name its own preset as its default and this block is retired.

proof.description: The trust-signal row (logos, ratings, counts) rendered under the CTAs. Free-form markup from the `proof` prop sits inside it.

surface.description: The panel a split hero renders its `proof` markup into, as the second column.

media.description: The split layout's image. Its crop is design, not structure: `sizing.aspect-ratio` takes `auto`, a number, or `16/9`.

safe_to_edit: ../../assets/css/components.css (COMPONENT: hero section — STRUCTURAL CSS ONLY: layout scaffolding, wrapper geometry and accessibility affordances. No colour, type, size, spacing, border, shadow or aspect-ratio value may be added there; every one of those belongs to a role above.)
